name: pwd
description: Print the full path of your current directory.
exercise: Change to your home directory with cd ~, then print its full path.

name: ls
description: List directory contents. -l shows details; -a includes hidden entries.
exercise: List your home directory including hidden files, with human-readable sizes.

name: cd
description: Change the shell's current directory. cd - returns to the previous directory.
exercise: Go to /tmp, return with cd -, then confirm your location with pwd.

name: mkdir
description: Create directories. -p also creates missing parent directories.
exercise: Create a projects/demo directory inside ~/linux-practice, then list it.

name: find
description: Search a directory tree by name, type, or other conditions. Quote patterns so the shell does not expand them.
exercise: In a practice folder, find only directories no more than two levels deep.

name: cat
description: Print files or combine their contents. -n adds line numbers.
exercise: Print /etc/os-release with line numbers and identify the distribution name.

name: grep
description: Print lines matching a pattern. -n adds line numbers; -i ignores case.
exercise: Filter three sample lines to show only those containing error, regardless of case.

name: sort
description: Sort lines of text. -n sorts numbers by value; -u removes duplicate lines.
exercise: Sort the numbers 9, 100, and 2 in descending numeric order using -nr.

name: sed
description: Transform a text stream. A substitution changes matching text in the output; these examples do not edit files.
exercise: Replace every occurrence of cat with dog in a sample line using s/cat/dog/g.

name: awk
description: Process text as records and fields. By default, fields are separated by whitespace; $1 is the first field.
exercise: Print only names whose second field is greater than 3.

name: ps
description: Show a snapshot of running processes. Output can include the process ID, parent ID, and command.
exercise: Find your current shell's process ID and parent process ID using the second example.

name: top
description: Display a live view of processes and resource use. Press q to quit the interactive view.
exercise: Open top, identify a process using CPU, then exit with q.

name: pgrep
description: Find process IDs by name. -a includes the full command line in the output.
exercise: List processes owned by your user. An empty name search simply means no match.

name: jobs
description: List background or stopped jobs belonging to the current shell. -l also shows process IDs.
exercise: Start a short sleep in the background and inspect it with jobs before it finishes.

name: kill
description: Send a signal to a process. TERM asks it to stop gracefully. Use only the disposable sleep process in this example.
exercise: Run the example, then use jobs to check that your test sleep has ended.

name: chmod
description: Change file permission bits. u means owner, g means group, and o means others.
examples:
touch practice-permissions.txt
chmod u=rw,go= practice-permissions.txt
ls -l practice-permissions.txt
exercise: In a practice folder, make a new file readable and writable only by its owner.

name: umask
description: Show or set the permission mask used when creating files and directories. A subshell keeps the example's change local.
exercise: Run the second example with a new filename and inspect its owner-only permissions.

name: id
description: Show user and group IDs. -un prints the current username; -Gn prints group names.
exercise: Print just your username, then list the groups you belong to.

name: stat
description: Display file metadata, including permissions, ownership, size, and timestamps.
exercise: Inspect a file in your home directory and identify its owner and permission bits.

name: test
description: Check a condition via its exit status. -r checks readability, -w writability, and -d whether a path is a directory.
exercise: Check whether a practice file is writable and print a message when it is.

name: ip
description: Inspect network interfaces and routing information on Linux.
exercise: Identify the loopback interface and the default route, if one is configured.

name: ping
description: Send ICMP echo requests to test reachability. -c limits the number of requests.
exercise: Ping the local loopback address three times and read the packet-loss summary.

name: ss
description: Inspect network sockets. -l shows listening sockets, -t TCP, -u UDP, and -n numeric addresses.
exercise: List listening TCP sockets and identify their local port numbers.

name: curl
description: Transfer data from a URL. -I requests HTTP headers; -L follows redirects. Requires curl and network access.
exercise: Request example.com's headers and locate the HTTP status and content type.

name: getent
description: Query system name-service databases, including hostnames and user accounts.
exercise: Resolve localhost and compare the returned address with the loopback interface.

name: tar
description: Create or list archives. -c creates, -t lists, -z uses gzip, and -f specifies the archive file.
examples:
mkdir -p practice-archive
touch practice-archive/hello.txt
tar -czf practice-demo.tar.gz practice-archive
exercise: Create the sample archive, then list its contents without extracting it.

name: gzip
description: Compress a file. -c writes compressed data to standard output, keeping the original intact.
examples:
printf 'sample text\n' > practice-gzip.txt
gzip -c practice-gzip.txt > practice-gzip.txt.gz
exercise: Compress a sample file while keeping the original, then inspect its compressed size.

name: gunzip
description: Decompress gzip data. -c prints the result without deleting the compressed file.
exercise: Pipe a short sentence through gzip and gunzip and confirm it comes back unchanged.

name: zip
description: Create ZIP archives. -r includes a directory recursively. Requires the zip utility.
examples:
mkdir -p practice-zip
touch practice-zip/hello.txt
zip -r practice-demo.zip practice-zip
exercise: Archive a practice folder and inspect the filenames reported by zip.

name: unzip
description: List, test, or extract ZIP archives. Requires unzip and a ZIP file; create practice-demo.zip in the zip lesson first.
exercise: List and test a practice ZIP archive without extracting or overwriting files.

name: git status
description: Show the state of a Git working tree and staging area. Run inside a Git repository.
exercise: In a practice repository, compare the full status with the short status output.

name: git diff
description: Show changes. By default it compares working files to the staging area; --staged shows staged changes.
exercise: Edit a file in a practice repository and inspect its changed lines with git diff.

name: git log
description: Browse commit history. --oneline condenses each commit; -5 limits the output.
exercise: Find the newest commit's short ID and message in an existing practice repository.

name: git branch
description: List local branches or create a new branch. Creating a branch does not switch to it.
exercise: List branches and identify the current one, marked with an asterisk.

name: git show
description: Inspect a commit or another Git object. HEAD refers to the current commit.
exercise: Inspect the latest commit's author and the list of files changed.

name: man
description: Open a command's manual page. In the usual pager, / searches and q quits. Requires installed manual pages.
exercise: Open the ls manual, search for human-readable, then quit with q.

name: printf
description: Print formatted text. Use a fixed format string and pass values as separate arguments.
exercise: Print three filenames, each on its own line, using one printf command.

name: df
description: Show filesystem space usage. -h uses human-readable units.
exercise: Find the available space on the filesystem containing your current directory.

name: du
description: Estimate disk space used by files and directories. -s gives a total; -h uses readable units.
exercise: In a small practice folder, compare its total size with the size of each subdirectory.

name: wc
description: Count newlines, words, and bytes. -l counts newline characters; -w counts words.
exercise: Create three lines of sample text and check both their line count and word count.

name: touch
description: Create an empty file, or update the timestamp of an existing one.
exercise: Create three empty files in a practice folder, then list them with ls -l.

name: cp
description: Copy files or directories.
exercise: Copy a folder recursively with cp -r and compare both with ls.

name: mv
description: Move or rename files and directories.
exercise: Rename a file, then move it into a new subfolder.

name: rm
description: Remove files or directories. There is no trash — deleted is gone.
exercise: Delete a test folder with rm -ri so it asks before each file.

name: rmdir
description: Remove an empty directory.
exercise: Try rmdir on a non-empty folder and read the error message.

name: ln
description: Create links between files; -s makes a symbolic link (shortcut).
exercise: Make a symlink to a deep folder in your home directory and cd through it.

name: tree
description: Show a directory as an indented tree.
exercise: Show only the first two levels of a project folder.

name: file
description: Guess what kind of data a file contains.
exercise: Run file on an image, a script and a binary and compare the results.

name: realpath
description: Print the absolute, resolved path of a file.
exercise: Resolve a symlink you created with ln -s.

name: head
description: Show the first lines of a file (10 by default).
exercise: Print only the header row of a CSV file.

name: tail
description: Show the last lines of a file; -f keeps following new lines.
exercise: Follow a log file with tail -f while appending to it from another terminal; stop with Ctrl+C.

name: less
description: Scroll through a file page by page. q quits, / searches.
exercise: Open a long file, search for a word with /word and jump with n.

name: cut
description: Extract columns from each line.
exercise: Print just the usernames from /etc/passwd.

name: uniq
description: Collapse repeated adjacent lines; usually used after sort.
exercise: Count how often each word appears in a file.

name: tr
description: Translate or delete characters from standard input.
exercise: Convert a sentence to upper case with tr.

name: tee
description: Write output to the screen and to a file at the same time.
exercise: Run ls -l and save the output to a file while still seeing it.

name: diff
description: Show line-by-line differences between two files.
exercise: Copy a file, change one line, and diff the two.

name: xargs
description: Turn input lines into arguments for another command.
exercise: List all .txt files with find and count their lines using xargs wc -l.

name: paste
description: Join files side by side, line by line.
exercise: Combine two single-column files into one CSV.

name: htop
description: Interactive, colourful process viewer (CPU, memory, per core).
exercise: Open htop, sort by memory with F6, then quit with q.

name: nohup
description: Run a command that keeps going after you log out.
exercise: Start sleep 300 with nohup, log out, log back in and find it with pgrep.

name: fg / bg
description: Move a suspended job to the foreground (fg) or background (bg). Ctrl+Z suspends.
exercise: Suspend a running sleep with Ctrl+Z, resume it in the background, then bring it back with fg.

name: pkill
description: Kill processes by name instead of PID.
exercise: Start two sleep processes and stop both with one pkill.

name: nice / renice
description: Start a process with lower priority, or change it later.
syntax: nice -n N COMMAND / renice N -p PID
exercise: Start a long command with nice and check its NI column in top.

name: watch
description: Re-run a command every few seconds and show the output.
exercise: Watch a folder fill up while you create files in another terminal.

name: timeout
description: Run a command but kill it after a time limit.
exercise: Run sleep 30 with a 5 second timeout and check the exit code with echo $?.

name: lsof
description: List open files and which process holds them (also ports).
exercise: Find which process is using a given port on the DGX.

name: time
description: Measure how long a command takes.
exercise: Compare how long gzip and xz take to compress the same file.

name: chown
description: Change the owner (and group) of files.
exercise: Check a file owner with ls -l, then read man chown to see why it needs sudo.

name: chgrp
description: Change the group of files.
exercise: List your groups with groups, then change a test file to one of them.

name: sudo
description: Run a command as another user, usually root. Use with care.
exercise: Run sudo -l to see what you are allowed to run as root.

name: groups
description: Show which groups a user belongs to.
exercise: Check whether you are in the docker group on the DGX.

name: whoami
description: Print your current username.
exercise: Compare whoami with and without sudo.

name: wget
description: Download files from the web; resumes with -c.
exercise: Download a small file and resume an interrupted download with -c.

name: ssh
description: Log in to a remote machine or run a command there.
exercise: Run one command on the DGX without opening an interactive shell.

name: scp
description: Copy files between machines over SSH.
exercise: Copy a small file to the DGX and back.

name: rsync
description: Sync files efficiently; only changed parts are sent. Great for big datasets.
exercise: Sync a folder twice and notice the second run copies almost nothing.

name: ssh-keygen
description: Create an SSH key pair for password-less login.
exercise: Read your public key with cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (never share the private one).

name: hostname
description: Show the machine name and its IP addresses.
exercise: Check which node you are on after logging into the cluster.

name: nc (netcat)
description: Open raw TCP/UDP connections — handy to test if a port is reachable.
exercise: Check whether port 22 is open on a remote host.

name: dig
description: Look up DNS records for a domain.
exercise: Find the IP address of a website with dig +short.

name: zcat
description: Print the contents of a .gz file without unpacking it.
exercise: Search inside a gzipped log without extracting it.

name: xz
description: Compress with a high ratio (slower than gzip).
exercise: Compress the same file with gzip and xz and compare sizes with ls -lh.

name: git init
description: Turn the current folder into a new Git repository.
exercise: Create a practice repository in a new folder.

name: git clone
description: Download a repository with its full history.
exercise: Clone a small public repository and look at its log.

name: git add
description: Stage changes for the next commit.
exercise: Edit two files, stage only one, and check git status.

name: git commit
description: Record staged changes with a message.
exercise: Make three small commits and view them with git log --oneline.

name: git push
description: Upload your commits to the remote.
exercise: Push a new branch and set its upstream with -u.

name: git pull
description: Fetch and merge changes from the remote.
exercise: Change a file on GitHub, then pull it locally.

name: git switch
description: Change branches, or create one with -c.
exercise: Create a branch, commit on it, and switch back to main.

name: git restore
description: Discard working-tree changes or unstage files.
exercise: Break a file on purpose, then restore it.

name: git stash
description: Shelve uncommitted changes temporarily.
exercise: Stash a change, switch branch, come back and pop it.

name: git remote
description: List or manage remote repositories.
syntax: git remote [-v] / git remote add NAME URL
exercise: Show where your repository pushes and pulls from.

name: git merge
description: Combine another branch into the current one.
exercise: Create a merge conflict between two branches and resolve it.

name: echo
description: Print text or variable values.
exercise: Print your PATH, then append a line to a test file with >>.

name: history
description: Show previously run commands; !N re-runs number N.
exercise: Find the last ssh command you ran and re-run it with !N. Also try Ctrl+R.

name: alias
description: Create a shortcut for a longer command.
exercise: Add an alias to ~/.bashrc and reload it with source ~/.bashrc.

name: export
description: Set an environment variable for this shell and its children.
exercise: Set a variable, start a new bash, and check it is still there with echo.

name: env
description: List environment variables, or run a command with modified ones.
exercise: Find every variable that mentions PATH.

name: which
description: Show which executable runs for a command name.
exercise: Check which python is used before and after conda activate.

name: type
description: Tell whether a name is an alias, builtin, function or file.
exercise: Compare type cd with type ls.

name: uname
description: Show kernel and system information.
exercise: Find out the kernel version and CPU architecture of the DGX.

name: uptime
description: Show how long the system has run and its load average.
exercise: Compare the load average with the number of CPUs from nproc.

name: free
description: Show used and available memory.
exercise: Check available RAM before starting a big data-loading job.

name: lsblk
description: List disks and partitions with their mount points.
exercise: Find which disk your home directory lives on (combine with df -h ~).

name: systemctl
description: Inspect and control system services.
exercise: Check whether the SSH service is running.

name: journalctl
description: Read system and service logs.
exercise: Show the last 50 log lines with journalctl -n 50.

name: crontab
description: Schedule commands to run automatically.
exercise: Write a cron line (not installed) that would run a script every day at 03:00.

name: date
description: Print or format the current date and time.
exercise: Create a folder named with today's date using mkdir run_$(date +%F).

name: source
description: Run a script in the current shell (keeps its variables).
exercise: Add an alias to ~/.bashrc and activate it without opening a new terminal.

name: nvidia-smi
description: Show GPU usage, memory and running processes.
exercise: Find which GPUs on the DGX are free right now.

name: tmux
description: Keep terminal sessions running after you disconnect; split panes.
exercise: Start a tmux session, detach with Ctrl+B then D, and reattach.

name: docker ps
description: List running containers (-a includes stopped ones).
exercise: List all containers on the DGX, including stopped ones.

name: docker run
description: Start a new container from an image.
exercise: Start a throwaway Ubuntu container with --rm and exit it.

name: docker exec
description: Run a command inside a running container.
exercise: Open a shell in a running container and look around.

name: docker logs
description: Show the output of a container.
exercise: Follow the logs of a running container and stop with Ctrl+C.

name: conda
description: Manage Python environments.
examples: conda create -n groot python=3.10 && conda activate groot
exercise: List your environments and check which python is active with which python.
